name: Land Surveying & Measurement

objectives.text: Identify basic surveying tools and their purposes, including a measuring tape, stakes, range poles, a level rod, and a builder's level
Determine a personal pace factor and use pacing to estimate distances across a field
Measure horizontal distances with a surveyor's tape by keeping the tape level and taut and marking each tape length with stakes or pins
Calculate the area of rectangular, triangular, and irregular plots in square feet and acres from measured dimensions
Demonstrate the correct setup and use of a builder's level or transit to establish a horizontal reference line
Explain the roles of a benchmark, turning point, backsight, foresight, and height of instrument in determining elevations
Measure elevation change across a field using differential leveling and record readings in a standard field notebook format
Calculate the grade, or percent slope, of a plot of land from measured elevation and distance data
Lay out square corners using the 3-4-5 method and stake out a rectangular plot or building site to given dimensions
Interpret contour lines on a topographic map to identify land features, determine point elevations, and calculate actual distances from map scale
Interpret metes and bounds and township, range, and section legal land descriptions to locate a parcel of land
Use compass bearings and taped distances to run a closed traverse around a field boundary
Conduct a grid survey of a field and record elevations at each grid point for contour mapping
Diagram a plot of land to scale from field survey notes, showing boundaries, bearings, and elevation contours
Evaluate the accuracy of a survey by closing a level loop or traverse and calculating the error of closure
Measure slope in the field and combine it with soil survey data to determine land capability classes as practiced in the FFA Land Evaluation CDE
Lay out a contour guide line or terrace line on the ground using a level for contour farming
Calculate cut and fill volumes needed to level or grade a site from survey elevation data
Apply survey data to design a drainage or terracing plan that manages water flow and controls erosion across a field

changes: Kept and reworded all six existing objectives, adding field notebook recording to differential leveling and erosion control to the drainage design. Added missing core surveying competencies: pacing, taping, area and acreage calculation, leveling terminology, 3-4-5 layout, topographic map interpretation, legal land descriptions, compass traverse, grid surveys, error of closure, field slope measurement for land capability (Land Evaluation CDE), contour line layout, and cut and fill volumes. GPS, GIS, drone, and sensor content was left to sibling sub-topics. AFNR codes were applied only from grade 9 up, where they genuinely match.
